summary: Extends duty-free treatment for imports from Haiti under the Caribbean Basin Economic Recovery Act until December 31, 2028, by amending eligibility rules and quantitative limits for apparel, restoring preferential status for certain articles, and allowing retroactive duty refunds for qualifying entries after September 30, 2025.

scores.thoughts: The bill extends duty-free import treatment for Haitian goods and adjusts related trade rules. It contains no provisions that authorize, increase, or decrease any form of government outlays, appropriations, or spending programs.

While the bill reduces tariff collections on specified Haitian imports, tariff policy is addressed under the separate trade_policy topic. The legislation does not engage with domestic tax rates, corporate taxation, or general revenue measures.
No provisions relate to healthcare delivery, insurance, public coverage, or market-based reforms.
The bill addresses only trade preferences for Haiti and contains nothing concerning firearms regulation or rights.
No immigration, visa, border enforcement, or refugee provisions are present.
The legislation is silent on reproductive health services or abortion access.
No defense authorizations, military spending levels, or related procurement changes appear in the text.
The bill does not address environmental regulations, emissions standards, or conservation measures.
No welfare, nutrition assistance, or social program eligibility rules are modified.
Nothing in the bill pertains to schools, federal education funding, or school choice.
The legislation contains no drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance provisions.
No sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform measures are included.

The core purpose is to extend duty-free treatment for Haitian apparel and other goods under the Caribbean Basin Economic Recovery Act, adjust quantitative limits, restore eligibility for certain articles, and apply the preferences retroactively. This directly advances preferential market access and reduces trade barriers, aligning strongly with free-trade and globalization objectives.
Any revenue effect from forgone tariffs is incidental and not addressed; the bill does not set fiscal targets or prioritize deficit reduction.
No provisions touch on legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
The measure uses trade preferences rather than direct financial assistance; it does not authorize, expand, or cut foreign aid programs.
The bill is unrelated to voting access, election administration, or voter ID requirements.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or platform oversight provisions exist.
Although apparel import caps are adjusted, the bill does not alter worker protections, union rights, or employer obligations.
The legislation does not engage with religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
